title: ASSIGN 100 TO IL; GOTO IL — dynamic GOTO, deleted from F95
sourceContent:
SUBROUTINE EXIT_PATH(MODE)
C     ASSIGN ... TO ... + GOTO is the OBSOLETE F77 dynamic-GOTO
C     idiom. The variable IL holds an unspecified type (label-like)
C     and GOTO IL jumps to whichever label IL was last ASSIGNed.
C     F90 marked it obsolescent, F95 deleted it. Real legacy code
C     still has it and the rewrite must replace it with structured
C     control flow.
      IMPLICIT NONE
      INTEGER MODE, IL
      IF (MODE .EQ. 1) THEN
         ASSIGN 100 TO IL
      ELSE IF (MODE .EQ. 2) THEN
         ASSIGN 200 TO IL
      ELSE
         ASSIGN 999 TO IL
      END IF
      GOTO IL
  100 RETURN
  200 RETURN
  999 STOP
      END
notes: Assigned GOTO is genuinely rare in modern review-able legacy code but appears in old NIST/MINPACK helper routines and IBM OS subroutines. The spec must capture the MODE -> path mapping; the rewrite is naturally a switch/enum but the analyst has to verify each label maps to the intended action.
